spec: Logo alone top-left, left third otherwise empty, link columns starting at about 33 percent of the width on a 200-230px pitch. 14px heads, 14px muted links on 28-31px rows. One short legal row about 100px below. Nothing else: no tagline, no socials row, no newsletter.

Four to seven equal columns across the whole container, no logo column, 14/500 heads, 14px muted links on 28px rows, on the page ground or one flat tone. Extra groups stack under short columns so the base stays level. A small status, theme or legal row closes it.

The densest thing on an airy page: 12px throughout in a narrow 980px column, bold group heads, about 26px pitch, five columns of stacked groups, hairlines top and bottom, numbered notes above, pipe-divided legal row below. Collapses to ruled accordion rows on phones. Hundreds of links stay calm.

Left block of about 300-430px holds logo, a two-line blurb and real proof: compliance marks, a live status dot, theme switch. Three to five link columns right, with small mono or muted heads, 14-16px links on 30-36px rows. Status line sits in the bottom row with a small green dot.

Signup is the first thing in the footer. Left block: 30px invitation, an honest line about what arrives, 42-48px field or one outlined Subscribe. Columns right from about 36 percent. Or a top row with title left and field right, a hairline, then columns. Never a field alone with no reason given.

The footer keeps the page's own grid: columns sit on the same guides or rails, split by 1px rules or dashed verticals that run through from above. Heads and links only, no fill change or a flat tone. Lines must meet the page edges. Works as a literal ruled table of 52px cells.

The white page ends in 24-40px bottom corners and lifts off a dark footer behind it, so the page reads as a sheet. The dark must sit behind the sheet, on body, or the corners show white. Six or seven columns of 14px links in the dark.

The footer is a dark or brand card inset 16-30px from the viewport on all sides, radius 8-24, about 1392 by 430 at a 1440 canvas. Columns pack to the right, wordmark bottom-left, the left two-thirds left empty on purpose. The page ground stays visible around it.

One full-bleed field of the brand colour, the largest flat colour on the page, held back until the end. All text in one tint of that field: white, or a dark of the same hue. Serif or display heads, 13-14px links, one lighter rule inset 16px. No second colour.

Links on top, then the wordmark at full container width as the very last thing, 220-380px tall, in full contrast, framed by hairlines. Use a trimmed SVG or size from ink bounds so it meets both margins exactly. Never stretch glyphs. Only a thin legal row may follow.

A very large wordmark set barely off the ground, about 4-8 percent of ink, and cropped by the page bottom or a hairline. It gives the footer weight without volume. Links stay in full contrast above it. Letters must fill the width, and the crop must look deliberate, cutting about a third.

evidence.name: Medusa622: Luxury Skin & Nails in Knightsbridge

spec: Edge-to-edge wordmark used as a window: halftone photo, moving video or customer imagery shows through the letters, or the letters are 1-1.5px outline with no fill. Use background-clip text or an SVG mask. The image must be busy enough to keep the letters readable at a glance.

evidence.name: Airpost: The Frontier Marketing OS for Frontier Companies

spec: The footer's largest element is a sentence, 76-170px, not a logo: a mission line, a repeat of the hero heading, or a plain ask. Small link columns or one legal row sit around it. Say something true and specific, or it reads as a slogan.

For studios and trades: no sitemap. Name, a labelled email and phone, address and social sit as text clusters on one ruled strip about 95px tall, or as label and value pairs at the left margin. Everything is selectable text, 15/20. Works at any size, up to a 70px address.

For anywhere people visit: phone, address and real opening hours are in the footer as text, not behind a link. Crest or script logo left, hours in three lines right, one row of links, thin rule, credit line. Say what is true: closed days, seasonal hours, separate kitchen times.

For few pages or a single funnel: one row under a hairline, about 60-110px tall, 12-14px. Copyright left, three links, status or socials right. Or a single centred sentence with dot separators. A short footer is honest. Padding it with columns of links that do not exist is what cheapens it.

A drawn or generated scene is the last image, cropped by the footer's top rule: a heap of mascots, a canvas ridge of hairlines, a horizon glow. Ordinary link columns sit below or over it. The scene must come from the brand's own world and stay under about 300px.

No separate block. The last photo or film runs to the page bottom and the footer is one row laid inside it: 12px tracked links, a round back-to-top, copyright right. The page ends on a picture. Needs a dark, quiet lower edge in the image, or a scrim drawn from it.

For regulated work, fine print gets a real layout: a 13px label in the left column, numbered notes in a 680px measure at 13/17 or 12/18, underlined links, bold run-ins on warnings, a one-step tint behind. Treat it as a document that someone will read.

Few links, set large: 20px rows on a 37px pitch, or 38-120px words stacked and right-aligned, sometimes numbered 01 to 06 with hairlines between. Type does the work, so no column heads. Only for sites with six to ten destinations.

Sitemap collapsed into ruled rows: 42-57px pitch, 15px labels, chevron or plus far right, 1px rules, in one column to the right or left of a form. Everything stays one tap away on phones, and the desktop page stops with calm. Hovered row turns full contrast.

The ending is one small made thing rather than a block: a tilted paper wall label, a desktop dock, a signature, a sticker back-link. Everything legally required lives inside the object. For personal sites and strong concepts only, once.

Left card about 310-430px holds what the app is for: QR tile, a phone crop, a rating with its review count. Three link columns to its right. The QR gives desktop visitors a real route to their phone. Only when the app is the main product.

Two or three uniform columns of square-cornered images with one caption row 8-12px below: name in ink, muted place or discipline, year, and a link or arrow right-aligned to the image edge. Gaps 16-24, no card, no border. The caption shares the image's left and right edges.

Rows change count on purpose: one full tile, then two, then three, all locked to the same gutters. Square corners, 20-50px gaps, 55px page margin or less. No hover chrome. The change of beat replaces any need for cards, and it looks curated rather than generated.

Title inside the image, bottom-left, inset 16-26px, on a scrim of about 80px rising from the base only. Tiles 16:9 or square, 0-8px radius, 8-24px gaps. Use when photographs are strong and dark enough at the foot. Never a flat overlay across the whole image.

One large tile beside a stack of smaller ones, with spans that vary row to row: 2+1+1 then 1+2+1 on four columns, deliberate holes allowed. 4-8px gaps, one small caption per tile. Different image scales give the eye a hierarchy that a uniform grid cannot.

Each work keeps its own proportions, uncropped. Set a max width per column, align the images to the bottom of the row so tops stagger and titles share one baseline, or centre them on the row midline. For art, architecture and anything where a crop would be a lie.

Edge to edge, 0-10px gaps, no captions, four to nine columns, and the page is simply the work. Fills the viewport so scale itself is the statement. Works for archives, community output and templates. Add a fade at the base if the wall is truncated, with one button on it.

Left-aligned to the page, running off the right edge with the next tile cut by the viewport: tiles 300-820px wide, radius 0-20, gap 16-20. A 21px caption under each, 36px round arrows below or above right. Native scroll with snap on touch. The peek is the affordance.

One slide about 930-1200px centred under the title, neighbours peeking both sides with a 12-16px gap. Below, a dot pager with an elongated progress dot and a small play-pause disc. Autoplay must have a pause control. For film, footage and big product pictures.

evidence.name: Alessandro Stella, Art Direction & Design Consultancy

spec: A horizontal band where every image has one fixed height and its own native width: 620px tall, widths 300-900, 100px gaps, white above and below. Driven by wheel or drag. Height is the only constant, so mixed work sits together without a crop.

Each project is one row under a 1px rule: large image left, short description mid, name right-aligned at far right, category on the row's bottom edge. Title stays top aligned beside tall media. Zones repeat exactly, so work of different shapes reads as one index.

The whole portfolio as a table: 40px rows, 14px text, columns title, type, client, year right-aligned, 1px rules, full width, no images until hover. Hovered row inverts to ink on ground and indents 14px. Reads as confidence: there is so much work that it needs a table.

A wide image with a narrow text column beside it, bottom-aligned: 920px photo plus 260px text, or an index of numbered titles beside one tall image. Rows may alternate. Label 11px, name 16px, body 14/1.6, arrow link. Row gap about 100px. Reads like a catalogue page.

One viewport holds one project; scroll swaps it in place. A centred 500-1170px frame stays pinned while neighbours enter from the edges, or a smaller clip rises over a large frame. Keep the swap under one screen of scroll, and give phones a plain stacked version.

Every project in one narrow column on the centre axis or a rail, images at natural ratio about 434-580px wide, 26-120px apart, no sections or headings. Name and place in a small column beside each. The length of the list is the proof.

Mixed sizes placed by hand across a loose grid, with lots of empty page: some cut-outs, some rectangles, each with a small mono number at its corner and one legend mapping numbers to names. Offsets of 40-120px. Needs real variety in the pictures.

Full-bleed row of about 320x240 photos at radius 12, each tilted about 2 degrees alternately, 35px gap, drifting slowly sideways, cut by both edges. One human moment on a technical page, or a hotel's scrapbook. Tilt under 3 degrees, and honour reduced motion.

Each project gets one thin horizontal slice of an image, about 80x19 or 230x12, in a list of names. Too small to read, so the colour marks tease the work and invite a hover that opens it up. An index with a pulse, for schools and portfolios.

Two or three recent posts as cards, then every other post as one-line rows: date and category 13px, title 14-15px, author right, 36-64px rows on hairlines. No excerpts in the ledger. A long archive stays scannable, and nothing needs pagination.

A newspaper front page: three columns of about 308/632/308px, a large lead tile and 32px title in the centre, stacks of 21px stories in the sides split by 1px rules with four-line clamps. Use only when you have at least five real stories at once.

One post runs full width as a split: 600px art left in a 10px frame, 20-30px title, excerpt and byline right. Below it filters, then a three-column grid of 16:10 thumbnails at radius 12. Needs a real art direction, since the lead image carries the page.

The whole index as a table: 36-42px rows on one line, or 81px rows with a 12px category and date line above a 14px title, author and read time right-aligned, 1px rule between. Filter tabs and search above. Add a 3 percent hover fill.

Rows at magazine scale: 212x285 portrait left, 50/60 serif title, category right-aligned to the top, 2px rules, about 367px pitch. Or a 38px headline and 540px cover with a date column. Type dominates the image, and each story gets a whole viewport's attention.

Text-only cells in a three-column grid: 13px date and category, 24/32 title, avatars and authors pinned to the base, about 240px tall. Separate with space alone and a 3 percent hover fill, or small outlined boxes, radius 0-10. No image means no stock photo problem.

The default: three columns of image-top cards, 8-16px radius, 12px meta, 16-20px title, short excerpt, 24px gaps. Fine for a resource library. It only works with a consistent image treatment, and pin dates to the base so they align across uneven text.

Left 120px rail of categories at 14px, active in bold, beside a two-column grid of cards with a pastel illustration tile, 22/700 title, 14px excerpt and byline. Calm for large archives. Works best with one illustrator, or one rule for every tile.

No card chrome at all. Three or four columns: image, then 20/500 title, one sentence ending in a link, 20-32px gaps, square corners or a shared small radius. Heights may vary. Sits between hairlines on a homepage as a small update section, not an index.

Homepage news as a rail: covers 350x197 at 8px gap starting on the page margin and bleeding past the right edge, title and date beneath, 32px square arrows above right, 'All news' beside them. Set on a tinted or dark band if the page needs a beat.

Active tile 818x460, then strips narrowing to about 188, 90, 42 and 8px, all the same height, radius 6, gap 16. Next stories compress at the edge, so depth is shown in one row. 40px arrow tiles top right, a white 40px title on the art. Stack on phones.

News as a bento: 8px gaps, tone cells with 16px radius and nested 12px images, varied spans, partner lockups on solid brand fills, each image carrying a 26px tinted chip with a mono category. Needs real logos and art. Kinds of tile must differ, not only sizes.

No stock photos: every post gets a cover from one system. Dotted field with a logo plate, line sketch with one accent, lettered cartoon or typographic poster. One rule, one palette, generated per post. It turns a feed into a publication, and is the cheapest way to look art-directed.

Filters as small text tabs, 13px, active a 28px filled pill or raised tone, search or RSS far right, directly under the title. Pagination is plain numerals with the current page a 32px pill. No dropdowns, no count badges, no boxed bar.

A dense dated feed: date divider bars, bracketed categories, handle and time in 8-11px, 14/21 bold titles, 12/18 copy, in up to four ruled columns. Reads as a live wire or a noticeboard. Only for communities and schools that truly post every day.

Two tracks: dates in a left rail of about 328px on a faint 1px vertical line with dots, entries in one 624-720px column, right third empty. No cards. About 110px of space and a 32px title mark a major release, 24px a minor one. Body 16/26, Copy link on each.

Three columns: 14px date, a 1px vertical rail with a 5px dot, a 763px entry column. Date and dot stick about 105px from the top while the entry scrolls, then hand over to the next. Entries may open with a wide art panel. The rail makes time physical.

A sticky rail of years and months beside the feed: 24/500 year with chevron, 15px months, active month ink with a 3px bar. Main column: 14px date, 44/700 title, version pill, lede, two-column sections, then a Shipped by row of 32px avatars. For long histories.

Each release is a ruled row: date in 12px mono caps, 32/400 title and tag chips in a left column of about 400px, screenshot and body in the right column. About 120px padding, hairline between. Reads as a catalogue of real product, so the screenshots must be real.

Dense and factual: 12px date column, version or title 18/500, then rows labelled New, Changed or Fixed in a 12px left column, 14px text, platform subheads in bold. Filter chips on top. For tools whose users read release notes to decide whether to upgrade.

Four latest updates on a shared horizontal rail across the content width: 8-12px dots at about 336px pitch, newest coloured, rest grey. Under each: 15/500 title, 14/20 copy clamped with an ellipsis, 13px mono date. 'View all' below. Compact proof that the team ships.

Each release is a card in a two-column grid: a 16:9 tint with one icon and a thin motif, or a cropped UI on a tint, then 12px date and a 14/500 title that lists items with commas. Scan by colour. Use one tint family, with at most five hues.

Per-day headings 14-16/600 over a 1px rule, a muted line when nothing happened, incident title in a warning colour, then updates with a bold status lead word and 12px timestamp. Plain, complete and honest. Trust comes from showing the empty days too.

A personal or project history: name with a small arrow, date range right-aligned on the same baseline, 13px role beneath, a paragraph, about 60px between entries, no dividers. Or live commit rows joined by a 2px line, the oldest fading to 30 percent.

Hours as body text, not fine print: 18-20/36, day in a fixed 160px column, time left-aligned in the next, no rules between rows, 1px rules between sections. Then address, a linked phone number, two outline map buttons, a map or photo at 50 percent. Say holiday hours and last entry.

A solid brand card with a title and seven day rows, 15px bold days on 36px rows, 7-on-4 dashed leaders running to the time, beside a real map tile of equal height and radius. Group equal days and show split shifts on two lines. The card is the page's one loud object.

Only what matters today, along the foot of the hero: bold 12px OPEN TODAY over the hours, the address, one action arrow, split by 1px slanted rules. Computed from a schedule, in the visitor's frame. The full table lives on the visit page.

Three columns of quiet cards: 16/600 name, 14px two-line address, clock icon with hours, then View and Order as a pair of 40px buttons pinned low. Group by state with a count and a jump select. Handle Coming soon and Temporary hours in the same slots.

Each venue gets a story: alternating rows on a tinted panel, 30px name, two paragraphs, a 4:3 interior photo, then icon rows split by hairlines for address, transport, today's hours and phone, then View and Book. For places where the room is the reason to come.

One column per office: a thin 105px live analog clock or a grey local time, city at 32-40/600, role label, address and linked phone at 16px, on a 345px pitch. Wraps to two up on phones. Live time turns a list of addresses into proof of a real team.

A list of places with no map: city name then two lines of address, in even columns about 210px wide, or a loose staggered grid of grey tiles about 265 wide fading in. Or city names at 20px over film. Use when the fact of where you are is enough.

The map is a drawn figure, not an embed: pale land on one tone, radius 32, flat pins, and 1px lines rising to 24px city labels at staggered heights, with 'HQ' as a small outline chip and upcoming sites in grey. Say something a Google embed cannot.

A plain band above the footer: Hours, Address, Contact or Order in three columns, 11px caps heads, 12-14px text, day and time aligned, one small button. Everything a visitor needs without leaving the page. The cheapest thing on this list and the most useful.

Two sites treated as two rooms: full-width split panels in two colours with a 42/600 name, a live 'Closed now' status at top right, an aerial photo and a shared map whose pins switch the panel. Or each venue a bold title and times, with its own map alternating sides.

Today's real conditions as data: a small block with live weather and a garden camera link beside a list of booking actions, or a rail of locations each showing hours and live capacity as a bold percentage. Only with a live source.

A full plan-your-visit page: a sticky 11-14px sub-nav of Hours, Directions, Admission, Accessibility, then each as a section with a map tile at 40 percent, a price table, transport tiles and underlined links. Long, plain and complete. Every question answered in text.

Item name left, price right on the same line, description beneath. 16px caps or medium name, 19px or 14px description, about 80px per item, one or two columns, section head large with a heavy 8px rule or 1px rule. No leaders needed if the column stays under 680px.

Price runs inline after the name, as in print: 13px tracked caps name and price in one line, then a 16/24 serif description, 24px between items, 1px hairline between sections, centred featured dishes framed by rows of small diamonds. Two columns on a tinted paper ground.

One centred column about 420-700px on warm paper: 16px tracked caps name, 17px italic ingredients beneath, price inline or on its own line, script or caps section heads, a small OR between choices. Reads as the printed card on the table. For fine dining and prix fixe.

Full-bleed food photo bands of about 360px between courses, and a white 720px card with a soft shadow overlapping each band's foot. Inside, 13px caps course title, then centred run-in lines: bold name, ingredients, price. Text stays on one page while appetite does the selling.

Three columns of identical overhead plates, square, radius 20, gap 24. Name 24px caps, 18px ingredients, one allergen line, 'Order now' or macro columns. Consistent photography is the whole design: same angle, plate and light, so the eye compares food.

A menu landing page: a three-column grid of about 76px framed buttons, one per menu, in the place's own ornament, 20-22px condensed caps, stacking to one column on phones. Use when there are six or more menus, and link each to a real page, not a PDF.

For salons, clinics and trades: tinted panels at radius 24 in two columns, each a category with a 30px title, 16px service rows with right-aligned tabular prices on a 34px pitch, 13px notes under a row, a condition such as a patch test at the foot. A double frame adds care.

A catalogue as text: all items as a list of 14-56px names, some with a year in brackets, the current item's caption beneath, one image at a time beside it. Or huge condensed service names on a 54px pitch with arrows pinned far right. Reads as an inventory.

Each product gets a whole viewport: full-bleed colour or illustrated scene, about 620px art, a 72px title, a 12px caps two-liner, one button, an index badge and a small pager. For ranges of four to eight with real character. Always show a plain list view as well.

Two to four tabs above a shelf of packshots: 48px serif tabs with a dot, or 58px pills, one outlined box at radius 30 clipping a marquee of products. Tabs change the set in place, so a small range feels navigable. One action below.

A catalogue of many: stacked horizontal rails, 22/500 title with a 32px arrow beside it, seven cards at about 194px pitch, prev and next far right, about 24px between rows. Phone shows about 2.1 cards, so overflow is obvious. Consistent thumbnails carry it.

A programme as a list: about 115px rows on 1px rules, a 36px display title left, dates right in grey, no cards. Or a row with image, ticket type, price and a Buy button. For venues and events, the date is the design: sort by it and group past from future.
